settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Windows path is enclosed in double quotes before being embedded (lines 308-310)
doNormalize rejects/removes null bytes via failIfNullBytePresent (FilenameUtils.java line 355)
On Unix the path is passed as a separate argument (lines 412-413), not a shell string
Class and freeSpace-family methods are @Deprecated (lines 44-49, 146-147, 175-178) with a nio.file.FileStore replacement recommendation
candidates.description: FileSystemUtils.freeSpaceWindows() normalizes the caller-supplied path with FilenameUtils.normalize(path, false) and then embeds it into a single Windows command string: new String[]{"cmd.exe", "/C", "dir /a /-c " + normPath} (line 313), executed by openProcess() via Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmdAttribs) (FileSystemUtils.java around line 500+). freeSpaceUnix() places the path as a separate argv element after the DF binary (lines 412-413). Because the Windows variant passes the whole thing as one string to cmd.exe, any shell metacharacters that survive normalization (e.g. & | > < ^) would be interpreted by cmd.exe if an application forwards untrusted input as `path`. Root cause: command construction by string concatenation rather than using a fixed array of arguments with no shell. Preconditions: an application calls FileSystemUtils.freeSpace/freeSpaceKb (or freeSpaceOS) with a path derived from untrusted input, on a Windows host, and the input keeps cmd metacharacters after doNormalize. Counter-evidence: the Windows path is wrapped in double quotes (lines 308-310) and doNormalize removes null bytes via failIfNullBytePresent (FilenameUtils line 355) and collapses separators/dot-segments; the class and the freeSpace-family methods are @Deprecated with a recommendation to use java.nio.file.FileStore (lines 44-49, 146-147, 175-178); on Unix the path is a discrete argv element so shell metacharacters in it do not create a new command. The library is a utility and does not itself obtain untrusted input, so reachability depends on the consuming application. Missing evidence: no in-repo caller forwards untrusted input; no test demonstrates metacharacter injection; behavior of cmd.exe quoting vs. embedded metacharacters was not executed.
missing_evidence: No in-repo caller forwarding untrusted input to these methods was located
No test or runtime demonstration of metacharacter handling by cmd.exe quoting
Exact behavior of cmd.exe with quoted path plus special characters was not exercised
preconditions: Application passes attacker-influenced string as the `path` argument to FileSystemUtils.freeSpace / freeSpaceKb / freeSpaceOS
Execution occurs on a Windows host (os.name contains 'windows')
Post-normalization path retains cmd.exe metacharacters such as & | > <
